Here's what the search turned up for South Korea in October 2026. Most of the coverage is from the first three weeks of the month.

**North Korea and security**
- Ballistic missile activity: Al Jazeera reports that North Korea fires multiple ballistic missiles towards the sea, and South Korea's Joint Chiefs of Staff said one of the missiles launched from the Pyongyang area flew more than 900km.
- DMZ landmine incident: A landmine explosion injured three South Korean soldiers in the Korean Demilitarized Zone, and Seoul is demanding an apology while N Korea denies planting mines. Nikkei Asia reports that President Lee Jae Myung avoids pointing finger at Pyongyang despite results of investigation.
- Russia ties: South Korea's intelligence agency reported that North Korea recently transferred ballistic missiles to Russia for the first time in approximately one year, according to an AEI–ISW analysis.
- Newest weapons claim: SCMP reports that North Korea says it tested new torpedo with AI tech, dated October 17.

**Government and politics**
- Cyber security: Prime Minister Han Sung-sook has responded to consecutive hacking incidents in the financial sector by ordering a broad security overhaul, and police have opened a formal investigation.
- Parliament: The National Assembly's parliamentary audit begins today for a run of about a month., according to the October 6 SBS briefing.
- Cabinet vetting: A feature on Korea Pro discusses how South Korea's Cabinet vetting crises expose decades of presidential resets, following the latest reshuffle.
- Diplomacy: Al Jazeera reports that South Korea to recall Ukraine envoy in diplomatic row over POWs, and that Seoul pledges legal action over alleged fuel exports to Russia.

**Economy and markets**
- Stocks: Korea Pro reports that South Korea's stock rout raises doubts over durability of chip windfall, describing a five-day KOSPI sell-off.
- Currency: The won faces a new test as foreign bond buying loses momentum, with the WGBI entry ending in November.
- US investment: Nikkei Asia has a headline saying South Korea to build 8 nuclear power plants in US, invest $120bn. The page's date is ambiguous, though, so I can't confirm it is from this month.

**Society and other**
- Crime: An Incheon suspect stabbed eight people at a shopping centre, and the Justice Ministry has apologised after the suspect met his probation officer hours before the attack.
- Space: Nuri, the country's space launch vehicle, was set for its fifth flight carrying 15 satellites.
- Sports: Al Jazeera reports that South Korea signals military exemption cuts for athletes after Asian Games.
- Culture: The TV schedule includes new drama releases such as Make Me Tingle, which is awaiting release.

Some of these sources are commentary or aggregator pages, and a few have inconsistent dates, so check the original outlets for the latest details.

2026년 10월 셋째주(10월 12~18일) 한국 주요 뉴스를 검색 결과 기준으로 정리했습니다. 검색 결과가 제한적이어서 전체 뉴스를 빠짐없이 담지는 못했습니다.

**1. 코스피 급락과 서킷브레이커**
이번 주 가장 큰 경제 뉴스는 국내 증시 급락입니다. 주식시장에서는 반도체와 인공지능 산업에 대한 기대가 불안으로 바뀌며 주가가 급락했다. 13일 코스피는 5.5% 급락하며 장중 6,000선이 무너졌다. 이틀 뒤인 15일에는 반도체주를 중심으로 매도세가 확산하면서 시장 전체 거래를 일시 중단하는 서킷브레이커가 발동됐다.

**2. 중동 전쟁과 한국의 역할**
외교·안보 분야에서는 한국군의 중동 작전 확대 가능성이 새로운 쟁점으로 떠올랐다. 국제 금융 측면에서는 세계 주요 금융당국이 AI 투자 확대와 에너지 가격 상승이 물가와 금리에 미칠 영향을 경계하기 시작했다. 이와 관련해 이번 주 태국 방콕에서 열린 국제통화기금(IMF)·세계은행 연차총회에서도 세계 경제의 새로운 위험이 논의됐습니다.

**3. 인천 흉기 사건**
인천의 한 복합상가에서는 전자발찌를 착용한 남성이 흉기를 휘둘러 여러 시민이 다쳤다.

**4. 정부 정책**
- 금융위·법무부 등 44개 기관 9929명이 내년부터 세종으로 본격 이전할 예정입니다.
- 정부가 어구·어법 조업방식 규제를 2031년까지 절반으로 줄이는 방향을 내놓았습니다.
- 한국의 관광발전지수가 1계단 올라 12위를 기록했습니다.
- 주택 공급과 관련해 연말까지 수도권 주택 21만 8000~23만 5000호 이상 착공을 목표로 한다는 정책뉴스가 있었습니다.

**5. 해외 소식**
프랑스에서는 대규모 시위와 폭동이 이어졌습니다. 한 보도는 파리 명품거리 털리고 143년 시청 무너졌다...프랑스 '수십 년 만의 최악 폭동'이라고 전했습니다.

참고로 '셋째주'를 10월 12~18일로 보고 찾았습니다. 주간 정리 기사는 이 기간을 다루고 있습니다. 더 자세한 내용은 연합뉴스, 네이버 뉴스 등 주요 언론의 주간 뉴스 페이지에서 확인하시길 권합니다.

North Korea's October 12, 2026 launch matches your query. South Korea's Joint Chiefs of Staff (JCS) reported that at least one of the missiles flew more than 900 km.

**The October 12 launch**
- The JCS detected the launch at about 9:20 a.m. Korea time from the Pyongyang area. At least one of the missiles flew more than 900 kilometers.
- The number of missiles is reported inconsistently. The U.S. Pacific Command statement refers to two ballistic missiles, while the JCS described multiple ballistic missiles toward the East Sea.
- Japan's coast guard had first reported two unidentified projectiles, believed to be ballistic missiles, adding that both appeared to have already fallen.
- U.S. Pacific Command said "Based on current assessments, this event does not pose an immediate threat to U.S. personnel or territory, or to our allies."
- South Korea's Joint Chiefs of Staff said the launch was North Korea's 16th round of ballistic missile launches this year.

**Context**
- Tensions rose after a border mine blast last month that wounded three South Korean soldiers. Seoul said the landmines had been planted by North Korea and demanded an apology, but Pyongyang has dismissed this and accused South Korea of provocation.
- Kim Yo Jong described the October 3 launch as a test of an intermediate-range strategic missile.
- The October 12 launch came after South Korea's first publicly showcased test of a hypersonic missile.

**The earlier October 3 launch**
This was a separate event that is sometimes confused with the October 12 launch. The missile was fired from the Wonsan area in Gangwon Province at around 6:30 am and flew more than 700 km before falling into the sea, the JCS said. Some outlets described that object simply as an unidentified projectile or suspected ballistic missile.

The Justice Ministry apologised after a man wearing an electronic ankle tag stabbed at least eight people at a shopping centre in Incheon. The ministry also said it would review the suspect's supervision and the wider electronic monitoring procedures.

**The attack:** Police and fire officials said the 59-year-old attacked shoppers as he moved through the mall before business owners and bystanders subdued him. One victim was in life-threatening condition and received surgery at a nearby hospital. On October 15, 2026, the KOSPI hit a circuit breaker after chipmakers led a sharp selloff. Multiple reports agree on the core facts, though the exact percentages vary slightly.

**What happened**
- The KOSPI fell 8% on Thursday, triggering a circuit breaker for the first time in 2-1/2 months, as chipmakers tracked a technology-led Wall Street selloff after sticky US inflation data raised bets of further rate hikes.
- Etoday reported that the KOSPI plunged 8.06% to close at 5,524.53 and the KOSDAQ fell 8.01%, and the halt lasted 20 minutes.
- The halt marked the 10th activation of a circuit breaker on the KOSPI this year and the 16th in its history.
- Foreign investors net sold 3.971 trillion won in the KOSPI market, while individual and institutional investors were net buyers.

**Chip stocks**
- Reuters reported that Samsung Electronics fell 9.70 per cent and peer SK Hynix lost 11.35 per cent, after the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index dropped 4.3 per cent overnight.
- A German market commentary put the moves at about 10% for Samsung and 11% for SK Hynix intraday, and noted that Samsung Electronics and SK Hynix together account for more than 50% of the KOSPI's market capitalization, which is why the index is so exposed to chip stocks.

**Context**
- The KOSPI was headed for a seventh straight session of losses, its longest losing streak since September 2024.
- Volatility had been stabilising since authorities tightened regulations in July to curb a retail boom in leveraged single-stock exchange-traded funds introduced in May.
- Analysts said the market is reacting sensitively to whether capital raising will be sustainable and whether massive infrastructure investment will lead to real income, according to Mirae Asset Securities.

**Caveats**
- Some results I found describe other dates (such as an October 13 sell sidecar and a separate circuit breaker with a 10.84% drop), and one Herald article describes a Friday halt at an 8,198 index level that doesn't match the ~5,500 level on October 15. I left those out.
- Percentages and closing figures differ slightly between sources, so check an exchange source (Korea Exchange) for official numbers.

Here are the three biggest South Korea stories from **October 11–18, 2026**:

1. **Stock market crash:** On October 15 the KOSPI fell about 8% to around 5,525, which triggered a 20-minute circuit-breaker halt; Samsung Electronics and SK Hynix each lost roughly 10%, and the index had been falling for nearly seven straight sessions as investors grew less confident about the chip and AI boom. [Source](https://longbridge.com/en/news/301923082)

2. **North Korean missile launch:** On October 12 North Korea fired several ballistic missiles from the Pyongyang area into the East Sea, and at least one flew more than 900 km, at a time when tensions were already high after last month's landmine blast at the border wounded three South Korean soldiers. [Source](https://www.koreatimes.co.kr/southkorea/defense/20261013/us-pacific-command-says-n-korea-fired-2-ballistic-missiles-reaffirms-defense-commitment)

3. **Incheon mall stabbing:** A 59-year-old man wearing an electronic ankle tag stabbed eight people at an Incheon shopping centre about two hours after meeting his probation officer, and the Justice Ministry apologized and ordered a review of how it monitors offenders. [Source](https://www.scmp.com/news/asia/east-asia/article/3370755/south-korea-shopping-centre-stabbing-leaves-8-injured)

I chose these three myself. Other news from the week included a string of hacking attacks on financial companies, after which the Prime Minister ordered a security overhaul, and the National Assembly's month-long audit of government agencies, which is still underway. Some figures, like the exact size of the KOSPI drop, vary a little between sources.
